summary: Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He was a lecturer at Bukkyo University in 1998, becoming associate professor at Soka University and editor-in-chief at IRIAB in 2000.

Norman Yoffee is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Northwestern University (~1962–1966) and Yale University (~1966–1973). He held posts at the University of Arizona (1972–1993), the University of Michigan (1993–2010), and New York University (2010).

Norvin Hein (1914–2011) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Franklin Edgerton from ~1946 to 1951 and served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University (~1950–1985).

Nosei Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University (1986–1988). He held posts at Daegu University (1988–1992), the Institute for Religious Culture, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, the Buddhist Cultural Institute, and Ryukoku University.

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He served as associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo from ~1986 to 2006.

Noémie Verdon works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne (~2009–2015) under supervisors Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and committee members Michio Yano and Blain Auer. She held a post at Kyoto University.

Nyanaponika Thera (1901–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon. He served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society from ~1958 to 1988 and taught Bhikkhu Bodhi and Donald K. Swearer.

Nyingcha Duoji is a Tibetologist who studied at Boston University and Harvard University (~2008–2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, Mark C. Elliott, Gendun Sherab, and committee members Janet Gyatso, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Michael Witzel.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Katok Monastery and under teachers including Penor Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, later teaching numerous prominent students.
Nyoten Jimbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University from ~1925 to 1946.

Olaf Hansen (1902–1969) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1945), the University of Jena (~1948–1950), and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969).

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna in 2009 under Ernst Steinkellner, and later served as a professor at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Paris (~1946–1948), Harvard (~1948–1950), and Princeton (~1950–1955). He held faculty posts at the University of Michigan (~1954–1969) and Harvard University (~1969–1990).

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and as Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from ~1888 to 1892.

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS under William Stede. He taught at Ceylon (1936–1943), the University of Pennsylvania (1963), Harvard (1966–1967), and Smith College (1967).
Oliver Philipp Frey is a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Vienna and later held a post there.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1925–1928) and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~-1939), later holding posts there (~1959–1970) and at Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

Olle Qvarnström is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Lund University (~1982–1989) under Tord Olsson, as well as Copenhagen, Harvard, and Washington, and held a post at Lund University around 1990.

Om Prakash is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Delhi (~1962–1967) under Dasharatha Sharma, was a senior lecturer at Kirori Mal College until 1961, and was professor of economic history at Delhi (~1967–2005).

Orna Almogi is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and under supervisors David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen (~1999–2003). She held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and the University of Hamburg (~2003).
